title: ethan-morales-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-11
content:
Evals / quality scratchpad - quick regression notes

Purpose:
- Quick personal notes while triaging a suspected regression in conversational coherence after merging quantized-kernel updates into serving runtime.
- Save sample outputs, ad-hoc rubric, and next steps so Maya/Sam can pick up.

Summary (top-line):
- Regression seen for conversational multi-turn statefulness on long conversations (> 800 tokens).
- Affected builds: model-serving v1.4-quant (rolling since 2026-03-08). Baseline: v1.3-full-fp16.
- Failure mode: context window trimming / incorrect KV-cache re-use -> persona/context hallucination and occasional repetition.
- Severity: medium (degrades UX, not catastrophic for stop-responses)

Quick metrics (rough):
- Coherence score (ad-hoc): v1.3: 0.86 avg (n=50), v1.4-quant: 0.62 avg (n=50)
- Repetition rate (n-gram repeat within last 200 tokens): v1.3: 2.4%, v1.4-quant: 9.8%
- Latency p95: v1.3: 320ms, v1.4-quant: 280ms (wins on latency)

Ad-hoc rubric used for quick scoring (1-5, 5 best) - keep simple for triage:
- Relevance (does reply address user prompt?): 1-5
- Context retention (keeps details from earlier turns): 1-5
- Fluency (grammatical / natural): 1-5
- Repetition (low = high score): 1-5
- Hallucination (factual innocence): 1-5
Notes: final score = mean of five dims. For the quick run I rounded to two decimals.

Representative prompts + outputs (copied verbatim from harness run)
- Prompt (multi-turn):
  T1: "Hi - I'm Alex, I work in product at Redwood. Yesterday we decided to prioritize the streaming widget for release."
  T2: "Can you remind me what we planned for the UI text and the error fallback?"

- v1.3-full-fp16 output (condensed):
  "Sure Alex - plan was: show inline spinner, after 10s show `Try again` CTA and fallback to cached response if available. Error text: 'Network hiccup - try again'. Also keep last 3 user messages in the context if the session is active."
  Notes: retains persona (Alex), references cached response plan -> good context retention.

- v1.4-quant output (condensed):
  "We will display a loading indicator and then fall back to a default message saying the action failed. The UI will show suggestions like 'Retry' or 'Contact support'. Also we can clear older context to save memory."
  Notes: drops specific 10s threshold, suggests clearing context (different behavior), loses 'Alex' reference in followup.

Short analysis of sample:
- v1.4-quant tends to prefer generic fallback text and less application-specific details. Could be due to: aggressive prefix compression / KV cache trimming in quant path or a subtle tokenization shift in quantized embeddings.

Observed patterns across ~50 samples:
- Loss of entity anchoring (user name, role) after 5-8 turns in v1.4-quant (rare in v1.3).
- Increased repetition when conversation switches topic quickly (topic boundary confusion).
- Slightly shorter responses on average (~10% tokens fewer).
- Latency improvement consistent (~10-15% p95 improvement) - cost/latency tradeoff obvious.

Immediate hypotheses to test:
1) KV cache pointer arithmetic bug in quant codepath -> run unit tests for KV index offsets, reproduce with deterministic seed. (Maya to help instrument).
2) Tokenization differences due to custom quant ops -> compare tokenized sequences between branches for same inputs.
3) Batching behavior change -> quant path may batch differently and cause partial context mixing; reproduce single-request isolated runs.

Quick reproduction steps for next run:
- Run harness with the same 50 seed prompts in isolated single-request mode (no batching) against v1.3 and v1.4-quant.
- Dump tokenized inputs + kv-cache snapshots at each generation step (enable VERBOSE_KV=1).
- Collect topk token probs for last 3 tokens to see distribution skew.

Notes / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Maya: add deterministic harness config and upload logs to linked GH PR (PR #312).
- [ ] Sam: add unit test for KV pointer math (see JIRA-EVALS-234).
- [ ] Me: run quick isolate run and attach sample diffs to Confluence page.
- [ ] Decide on rollback policy if we confirm regression: (A) revert quant kernel merge, (B) patch kernel with fix, (C) rollout config to disable quant path for long-convo routes only.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is this degradation more pronounced on longer sequences only or also on few-shot prompts with long contexts? Need to expand sample set to include both.
- Do embeddings/semantic caching behavior change between branches? Might influence long-term coherence via cached prefix reuse.

Helpful links / references:
- PR with kernel changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 (suspect area)
- Evals harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/main/harness
- Ticket: JIRA-EVALS-234 (KV cache pointer investigation)

Scratch thoughts (brain-dump):
- If kernel changed padding/truncation semantics for block-aligned matrices, we might be silently dropping tokens at internal boundary -> shows up as context loss.
- Quick smoke: feed a long prompt with repeated sentinel token and see if token count in model internals matches input token count.
- Consider adding a short-lived feature flag to disable quant path for customer-facing long-convo endpoints while we triage.

Bottom line (for now):
- There appears to be a quant-related regression affecting context retention in long conversations. We have a prioritised triage path (above). I'll run isolation tests today and paste logs here.

-- Ethan

(Notes to self: keep this doc as ephemeral scratchpad. Move cleaned findings to Confluence once we have deterministic repro.)
